description: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: `<Declaration>.<field>` as the label, the comment's first paragraph as the definition. Generated by folio-assistant-core/scripts/glossary-extract.ts; not curated, and never hand-edited: a person promotes a term by authoring it in a glossary of their own.

terms.definition: Where the bytes are, when they are anywhere. Required when `materialized`: a materialized asset with no locator is a claim that something is here without saying where, which is the one shape the state exists to rule out.
What it is, in a few words, so a reader of the record can follow it.
Stable identifier — a bib-slug, a block id, a path.
Who adjudicated, and of which kind. An outcome with no adjudicator is indistinguishable from a default.
The chosen code. Must be one of `codes`.
The enum in force when this was adjudicated.
Optional structured debate record formalizing debate rounds conducted prior to the adjudicator's verdict (SWE-Debate / 2507.23348v1).
Why, as markdown. REQUIRED, and never empty.
The request this answers.
Everything the adjudicator is shown, and **nothing else is**.
The permitted answers — the owner's *"list of judgement codes"*.
Stable id, so an outcome can point back at the exact question asked.
The question, as markdown.
What choosing this code means. Required — see the type docstring.
Regions blanked out of these bytes before they were written.
Its own materialisation state. An item may be referenced while one of its bitstreams is materialised — which is exactly the worked example.
Pixel dimensions, where the bitstream is a raster.

How many children the SOURCE says this container has — not how many are modelled here. The gap between the two is the whole point of a catalogue by reference, and a renderer that counted `children.length` would report the model's size as the collection's.
The source system's own word for this node — `community`, `collection`, `set`, `prefix`. Display and provenance only; nothing branches on it.

The node's Handle, where the source mints one — PREFERRED over any host URL for resolution ({@link resolvableIri}). Recorded only when read off the source; never derived for a node that shows none (a DSpace community or collection has a Handle upstream, but none is recorded here until one is read).
The local library slug, where this item has been ingested. Present iff something under `library/` corresponds.
The item's metadata record, by reference to a `folio-dublin-core/v1` file.
Containment, as paths from the catalogue root. A LIST, because an item may be mapped into several collections and because the breadcrumb on the one measured item is four levels deep.
How the numbers above were arrived at. A denominator with no provenance is a denominator nobody can check.

What survives if the SOURCE goes away, stated per node kind — not only for bytes already copied (bean `08u4`). The `sourceLoss` GATE is asked only of a materialization; a referenced node never meets it, so without this the answer for 10 of 13 nodes was silence.
The source system, e.g. `DSpace 7`.
FILES upstream, where the source publishes that separately.
ITEMS upstream — the things a person cites, not the files they are made of.
Why this region is masked, in a person's words. Never generated.
Exclusive.
Exclusive.
Manifest path relative to the folio root.
Zero-based position within that section.

The section listing it: `{manifest dir}::{section label | title | #n}` (written with braces: angle brackets here were published as an escaped HTML `section` tag and failed the site build). Absent when no manifest lists the block — an orphan, which is itself worth a reviewer's attention and is not guessed at.
The same, rendered by the platform's Markdown renderer.
The Markdown source, exactly as committed.
Every block that differs, in head reading order, then removed blocks.
Folio root, relative to the repository root.
Default `origin/main`.
The contributed builders, so contributed (DAK) blocks are blocks too. See {@link snapshot}.
Folio root, relative to `repoRoot`.
A ref, or {@link WORKTREE} (the default) for the files on disk.
Repository holding the folio.
The commit it resolved to; `null` for the uncommitted working tree.
What was asked for — `origin/main`, a branch, or `worktree`.
A contributed (structured) kind's manifest fields, read as text (bean f327). Never serialised.
Absolute path of the prose sidecar, when there is one. Never serialised.

`literal` when DCMI gives the term the range `rdfs:Literal` or gives no range and the value is prose; `resource` when the range is a class (Agent, Location, LinguisticSystem, …) or DCMI says the term is "intended to be used with non-literal values".
A syntax encoding scheme the values are in, by the field's own name. Becomes a datatype (JSON-LD) or `xsi:type` (XML).
The local name under `http://purl.org/dc/terms/`.
A vocabulary encoding scheme the values are members of. Becomes `dcam:memberOf` (JSON-LD) or `xsi:type` (XML).
The namespace prefix. `dc` throughout the measured record; DSpace also mints `dcterms`, `local` and others.
Every value, in the order the source gave them. Never collapsed.

The authority record this value is controlled by, where there is one. `dc.subject.mesh` is a controlled vocabulary with its own resolution; a free-text keyword is not. Keeping the distinction addressable is what lets a later tool ask "which of these subjects can I look up".
BCP 47, as DSpace stores it (`en`, `en_US`, `fr`).

The repository's own identifier for the item — a DSpace UUID here. NOT the library slug: the slug is derived downstream and is the weakest of the three identifiers this repository holds for the one worked item.
Where this record was read from, and when. A metadata record with no provenance is the `source: null` defect bean `r1lz` was opened over, wearing a different hat.

The id of the statement this one was derived from, when it was: a scenario candidate written from a recommendation names that recommendation, so a reviewer can check one against the other. Its `source` is still the library source, never the other statement.
Stable within the list; the anchor the statement's row is published under.
The kind the extraction gave it: recommendation, requirement, candidate, …
The statement as captured, verbatim. Never paraphrased here.
Its review state, as the extraction records it: published as is.
What the list is, in a reader's words: a heading for its part of the page.
URL prefix of the library viewer: an entry's link is `<entryBase>/<libraryId>/`.
The page to write.
URL prefix of the sources: a section's link is `<sectionBase>/<repo-relative section file>`.
The statement lists, in the order their parts appear.
The content type's look, written after each table (for example a kramdown class).
The DECLARED NAME of the instance holding the library; absent means this instance.
The library entry: `library/<libraryId>/`.
The page (or slide) the statement was read from, in the source's own numbering.
The section the statement was read from, when the extraction knows it.
dcterms:hasVersion.
The scheme's local id: the tail of its IRI.
The licence the terms are published under: an SPDX id or a URL.
External concept IRIs this glossary lists without copying: a `skos:Collection`.
dcterms:modified, a date.

The terms are in a LOGICAL order, each defined only by terms above it, and a reader should meet them in that order — not alphabetically. The owner, 2026-09-29, of bootstrap's terms: keep "logical rather than alphabetical order". Published as a skos:OrderedCollection.
dcterms:source: what the terms were drawn from.
The subject area this scheme's translations bind in ({@link SubjectSchema}): `dcterms:subject`.
Local term ids or absolute IRIs.

A note for the editors, not part of the meaning (`skos:editorialNote`): the document's own marks such as "Under review" or "To be included before publication". A table drawn from the glossary prints it in brackets after the definition, as the document does (smart-ra Q-RAC-8 A).
The thing the concept is about, an organization or an architecture element ({@link FocusSchema}): `foaf:focus`.

The concept's IRI when its defining vocabulary already mints one. The glossary then DESCRIBES that concept — its labels, translations, order — rather than minting a second IRI for the same term. Owner, 2026-09-30 (bean `xsqm`, "one SKOS", option A): bootstrap's terms are `<bootstrap>/ns/Node`, not also `…ns/glossary/terms/node`.
The schema or standard that defines the term (rdfs:isDefinedBy).
The code. SKOS's own word for it.
Required for `could-not-extract`: a person must be able to act on it.
Local ids of the terms this definition USES — what a reader must know first (dcterms:requires). In an `ordered` glossary each must come earlier; the scheme refuses one that does not.
Where the term came from: a repository path (with #anchor) or an IRI.
Overrides the scheme's {@link SubjectSchema subject area} for this term.
Per locale, whether this term's translation is signed off. The translation itself is in the scheme's `.po`, never here: this records only who stands behind it. A locale not listed is `unofficial`.
Who decided, applied to every gate that does not name its own `decidedBy`.
When the copy expires; recorded as `expiresAt`.
The size budget, in bytes. Absent: {@link DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES}.
Path relative to the part's `tree/` (or the licence's own name).
A held SUBGRAPH: one record per file under `tree/`.
The upstream licence, copied beside the tree so its notice travels with the copy.
The pin the part was asked at — the subscription's `ref` when it was written.
Present iff the part stayed referenced.
The `subscriptions[].id` this part belongs to.
Nodes in the subgraph's transitive membership, and subgraphs under it, as counted from the file.
The pin the file was fetched at — the subscription's `ref` when it was written.
The one gate that applies: MEASURED bytes against `maxBytes`.
`materialized`: the file is here; `referenced`: the size cap stopped it, and `size` says so.
A purpose is asked FIRST; a part with none cannot have its gates judged.
The DECLARED NAME of the instance holding the corpus — not a path.
A sha256 over the build inputs, where the builder can produce one.
The revision of the source the artefact was built from, e.g. a commit sha.
The compiler and its version: `leanprover/lean4:v4.24.0`, `sushi 3.12.0`.

Why. REQUIRED on every verdict including `permitted`, because "we checked and it is fine" and "nobody looked" are indistinguishable from a bare `permitted`, and this whole module exists to keep such pairs apart.
Who or what decided, and when. A verdict with no date cannot be re-checked.
Bytes held locally. Absent means not measured, which is not zero.
Bytes the WHOLE remote collection holds, where it is known. This is what makes a `size` gate answerable: 3 items of 361.55 GB is a fraction, and "3 items" alone is not.

When this copy expires. Absent on a `working` copy is a `retention` finding, not a default of "forever". Absent on an `archival` one is the SPECIFICATION — see {@link freshness}, which reports the two differently.
Required when `purpose` is `archival` or `both`.
Required when `purpose` is `compiled`, and only allowed then. See {@link CompiledInputsSchema}.
When this copy was last read. Absent means 'not recorded'.
Where the bytes landed, instance-relative. Present iff `materialized`.
When the local copy was taken, and against what upstream version.
Why the record cannot say more than it does.
WHERE THIS CAME FROM — see {@link SourceProvenanceSchema}.
Why the bytes were taken. Required on anything materialized — the gates mean different things under each.
Other plausible targets, for triage to choose between.
Why, in a sentence a triager can check.
A block or section label in the folio; null when unplaced.
The GitHub comment or issue it came from, when moved on GitHub.
The GitHub comment, issue or PR it came from.
Before/after deep links to the comment's anchor.
The staging preview of the change set.
"Table 3.1" / "Figure 2.2" as parsed from the line or comment.
The cell or phrase exactly as given.
Where the change is made, for a decision that changes the document.
GitHub issue holding this comment's discussion, once one is opened.

Categorisations the intake log carried, keyed by its column header and kept verbatim: a theme, a stakeholder type, a review question, a priority, a committee routing. Read, never re-coded, so a log can grow a column without a schema change.
"PC-0042": the number a committee and a commenter refer to.
The comment as written.
GitHub login of the committee member.
The issue or PR comment it was given in.
Stable pseudonym: a hash of the normalised email or name.
Only when `acknowledge` is true.
The intake batch: a file name, a form export, a letter.

The log's OWN number for the row ("No."), within its sheet. A review log is re-sent as it is worked, so a later copy is a different file with the same rows: this, with the sheet and the series, is what recognises them.
For a narrative: which passage of the letter this comment is.
The log this row belongs to, across the copies of it that are re-sent.
sha256 of the intake file, so a re-import is recognised.
For a GitHub comment: its URL.
`at` and `by` default to the transition's.
`at` defaults to the transition's.
The asset it was taken from: a DC record, a library manifest, a paper's references section. Repo-relative path or IRI.
The library asset that holds a copy of the work, when one is held. Repo-relative path or IRI.

The entry exactly as the citing document prints it, when no citation style reproduces that wording (a committee's own short form, two works in one entry). A reference list drawn from the node (`scripts/references-render.ts`) prints this text verbatim instead of formatting the CSL fields, so the KG stays the one source without changing a word. Not CSL: dropped from CSL-JSON exports.
Where the reference came from. Absent means `authored`.
Optional raw BibTeX or CSL-JSON / JSON-LD text to parse before applying explicit fields.
The section listing the block (the ChangeSet's form). The heat map's row for its comments (bean `qbfi`).
Decisions applied by this run, as `<decision comment id> → <review comment id>: <status>`.
A decision tag that could not be applied, and why: said, never silently dropped.
How many PR comments carried a decision tag, so they are not counted as conversation.
The review comment's id.
Everything after the header, trimmed: the reason.
Tagged but malformed: said, not dropped, so the reviewer can fix it.
Already ingested. Same id, so nothing new.
No tag: ordinary conversation. Counted so "nothing ingested" is explained.
GitHub's `author_association`: OWNER, MEMBER, COLLABORATOR, CONTRIBUTOR, NONE… Absent when not known.
The `<bpmn:process id>`.
The task's id in that process.
The head commit whose blocks the comments were anchored against.
Reviewers' per-block verdicts (`folio-review-verdict/v1`, bean `px0t`), ingested from the same PR comments. Default `[]`, so a file written before verdicts existed still reads.
The labels this comment was anchored to before a rename re-anchored it.

The block's content hash when the comment was ingested. `null` when the block was not in the head at all, so the comment was orphaned from the start. Recorded rather than refused, because a reviewer's words are kept.
GitHub's id of the conversation comment this was ingested from.
The head commit the comment was ingested against.
The 9gyz Decision that closed it. Required once resolved or adjudicated.

The PR conversation comments whose `resolve:` tag has moved this comment ({@link applyDecisions}), in the order applied. A rebuild applies each one once: the record, not the build count, says what has been decided.
The block the label names is gone. Kept and shown, never dropped. An anchor fact, not a status: the review process still decides what happens to the comment.
The edit-set's pull request.
`owner/name` of the repository the pull request is in.
GitHub login of the reviewer.
The lane they reviewed in: a role id from `roles.json`.
Everything after the header, trimmed.
`null` for creation.
A transition that closes a comment must name the Decision that closed it.
The changed blocks that need review, in ChangeSet order.
Whether the build was measured against its base.
Pages the build measured and the prediction missed, not reviewed since. Counted only when `measured` is `known`.
`GW_Covered`'s fact: review comments of kind `defect` still open or addressed.
Whether a rendered impact was given; when `absent` the three lists below are empty because UNKNOWN.
Verdicts on an OLDER version of what they are on, which therefore do not count.
Of those, the ones with no current verdict.
`GW_Covered`'s fact: changed blocks with no CURRENT verdict.
Inputs no renderer could place, with neither a current verdict nor a waiver.
Rendered pages (and data files) on the review list that nobody has reviewed at their current pin.
The predicted files and undetermined inputs, every renderer's, each pinned.
The build's measurement, when it was measured.
The block's content hash (a page's or input's pin) when the verdict was given. It counts only while current.
The head commit the verdict was ingested against.
`verdict-pr<n>-c<comment id>-<label>`: derived, so a re-run finds it rather than adding one.
Required for `waived`: why this block needs no review.
GitHub login.
The lane they reviewed in: a role id from `roles.json`.
Absent on verdicts written before pages could be reviewed: those are all on blocks.
A block's label, or a page's or an input's path, as `target` says.
Said, not dropped, so the reviewer can fix it.
